record.original_question: Let A be an n × n GKK τ-matrix. For each j = 0, ..., n, define c_j to be the average of all principal minors of A of order j, namely c_j = (sum of A[α] over all α with #α = j) / binomial(n, j). Must A satisfy Newton's inequalities c_j^2 ≥ c_{j-1}c_{j+1} for every j = 1, ..., n - 1?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A complex n×n matrix A is called a GKK matrix if (i) every principal minor of A is positive (so all principal submatrices have positive determinant) and (ii) A is weakly sign-symmetric, meaning that for every pair of index sets α, β ⊂ {1,…,n} with |α∩β| = |α|−1 = |β|−1, the product A[α∪{i}|β∪{i}]·A[β∪{i}|α∪{i}] of the two corresponding almost-principal minors (where {i} is the symmetric difference) is nonnegative. A GKK matrix A is called a τ-matrix if, in addition, for every principal submatrix B of A the spectral radius of B is an eigenvalue of B and equals the largest real eigenvalue of B (the "eigenvalue monotonicity" condition: ρ(A[α]) ≤ ρ(A[β]) whenever α ⊂ β).

For an n×n matrix A and an integer 0 ≤ j ≤ n, define
   c_j(A) = (1 / C(n,j)) · Σ_{α ⊂ {1,…,n}, |α|=j} A[α],
the average of all principal minors of A of order j (with c_0(A) = 1 and c_n(A) = det A).

Question: Does every n×n GKK τ-matrix A satisfy Newton's inequalities
   c_j(A)^2 ≥ c_{j−1}(A) · c_{j+1}(A)  for every j = 1, …, n−1 ?
artifact.status_search_result: Newton's inequalities are known to hold for M-matrices and inverse M-matrices (Holtz, Proc. AMS 2005). Subsequent work showed that GKK τ-matrices need not be stable, disproving several long-standing conjectures, but no source located explicitly resolves whether the Newton inequalities c_j^2 ≥ c_{j−1} c_{j+1} hold for all GKK τ-matrices. Status appears unresolved in the available literature.

status_evidence.title: M-matrices satisfy Newton's inequalities
status_evidence.snippet: Newton's inequalities are shown to hold for the normalized coefficients of the characteristic polynomial of any M- or inverse M-matrix.
status_evidence.claim: Newton's inequalities are established for M-matrices, a subclass; the analogous question for the broader GKK τ-class remained the motivating open problem.

status_evidence.title: Not all GKK τ-matrices are stable
status_evidence.snippet: A class of unstable GKK τ-matrices is described, disproving the conjectures concerning stability.
status_evidence.claim: Stability conjectures for GKK τ-matrices were disproved, but the Newton inequalities question is distinct and not addressed there.
